info.title: Playpencil API
info.description:
The `/v1` HTTP API of the Playpencil sandbox daemon (default `127.0.0.1:7070`).

**Compatibility.** Unknown request fields are ignored. Clients must tolerate unknown response fields and unlisted values, including notice codes.

**Errors** are RFC 9457 problem details, except the bodiless health `503`. An unreadable, malformed (trailing content included) or non-JSON body, or an unparseable query string, gets a bare `400`; any other invalid request gets `422` `invalid_input`. Integers must be plain JSON integers (no fraction, exponent or `-0`). `401` and `403` are reserved and not returned by this version.

Writes return `202`; read convergence from `status`. Timestamps are RFC 3339; binary data is base64.

**Environment.** `env` maps are written as `{NAME: value}` and read back as names only. A process gets the baseline, then the sandbox's `config.env`, then its own `env` (later wins); `PLAYPENCIL_*` names are removed and nothing is inherited. Baseline: `PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin`, `HOME=/root`, `TERM=xterm`, `LANG=C`, `LC_ALL=C`.

**Defaults.** Stop grace 5 s (flush, then kill). Reap tolerance 60 s.

post.description: Idempotent on `name`: the same namespace and configuration (defaults applied, `desired_state` ignored) returns the existing document; otherwise `409` with `existing_id`. A missing `config.network`, or a missing or unknown `config.backend` (with `available_backends`), is `422`.

patch.summary: Change a sandbox's target state or configuration.
patch.description:
`202` even when nothing changes.
- No `if_version`: `422`; stale: `409` with `current_version`.
- `network` (hot) is accepted in any state. `mounts`, `env` and `main` (cold) only when `state` is `stopped` and `desired` is `stopped` or a `reason` is set, else `409`; they take effect at the next start. `backend` and `backend_options` are immutable (`422`).
- `destroyed` is final (`409`). While a `reason` is set, changing `desired_state` needs `clear_reason` = `reason.id`, else `409`; configuration-only writes leave `reason` unchanged.
- Validation is all-or-nothing. `config` applies before `desired_state`; `network` is enforced before the response, and if that fails: `500`, the old policy stays and `desired_state` isn't applied.

get.description:
Server-sent events: `event` is `changed` or `notice`, `id` the cursor, `data` a `ChangedEvent` or `NoticeEvent`. Resume with the cursor as `since` or `Last-Event-ID` (preferred).

On connect: (1) with a cursor, the events after it are replayed, or a `gap` notice if they aren't retained; (2) the baseline at one cut (`changed`, `pin_registered`, `host_addresses_changed`; flagged `baseline: true`, with the cut `seq` and cursor); (3) `resync`; (4) live events, including changes made during the baseline. A policy change's `changed` event separates denials under the old and new policy. The buffer is bounded.

WebSocket upgrade to the streaming-link protocol (open processes, attach, control); its frames aren't described here. A stream whose owning link drops is held for the reap tolerance, then interrupted.

post.summary: Spawn a detached process in a sandbox.
post.description: A synchronous start failure is `422`; later failures appear on the record. Not ready: `409`.

delete.summary: Interrupt a process (TERM, grace period, KILL).
delete.description: The record turns terminal only on confirmed termination. Ended or superseded: `409`.

listeners.description: Concrete `addr:port`s the daemon listens on, the streaming link included; wildcard binds are expanded.

main.description: Its exit stops the sandbox (`exited` if clean, else `crashed`) and kills its descendants; some may escape on `BestEffort` backends. Absent: the sandbox is idle and exec-only, with exec-spawned processes unbounded.

ConfigPatch.description: Present members replace the current value wholesale; absent ones are unchanged.

ConfigRead.description: As written; members omitted at create are omitted.

namespace.description: Exact and case-sensitive; `"*"` is reserved; immutable.

expired_pin.description: Name whose expired pin caused the denial.
Name whose expired pin caused the denial.

dial.description: `egress_none`, `egress_allowlist`, `fs_workspace_confinement` or `teardown_confirmation` (`Strong`: verified empty; `BestEffort`: escaped descendants may survive).

InternalProblem.description: Policy not applied; the previous one is still enforced.

Mount.description: A host directory bound into the sandbox; `guest_path`s are unique. Access is limited to the daemon user's permissions and stays within the directory. Close-to-open consistency, POSIX locks, atomic rename. Unflushed writes can be lost on abrupt death; a graceful stop flushes them.

NetworkRead.description: As written; `mode` may take other values.

NetworkWrite.description:
`none`: nothing reachable. `allowlist`: only the entries. `all`: all egress; entries only grant host-local access.

Host-local addresses (loopback, link-local, the host's own, the daemon's) are reachable only via `host.internal` (an exact entry, never matched by a wildcard) or a covering address or CIDR, which keeps granting even if the host later acquires the address; guest loopback never reaches the host. Names match exactly, `*.name` proper subdomains only, addresses and CIDRs by prefix; TCP and UDP only. Only permitted names resolve (others get NXDOMAIN and a `deny` notice), to public addresses only (under `all`, also non-host special-use ones) unless a literal covers them; resolved addresses are pinned until TTL expiry or re-resolution.

Entries are `(name|*.name|ip|cidr):(N|lo-hi|*)` in canonical form, else `422`. Names: lowercase A-labels of `a-z0-9-`, no edge hyphens, `--` only in a leading `xn--`, labels ≤ 63 and names ≤ 253 octets (`*.` included), no trailing dot, last label not all digits. IPv6 bracketed in RFC 5952 form, no zone or IPv4-mapped; IPv4 without leading zeros; split at the last `:`. CIDRs without host bits; full-length prefixes written as the address. Ports 1–65535 without leading zeros, `lo < hi`; `N-N` written `N`, `1-65535` written `*`.

Writes apply atomically: on return, new connections and DNS use the new policy and flows it no longer authorizes are closed; a rejected write changes nothing. Pin expiry and host address changes re-check flows likewise. Processes that escaped a `BestEffort` teardown keep their old policy.

oneOf.description: A connection or DNS query was refused.
Ends the baseline, which follows any replay; later events are live.
A stop or destroy killed before the guest flushed; recent writes may be lost.

detail.description: Says when the sandbox isn't ready.

ProcessRecord.description: A process in a sandbox. Records don't survive a daemon restart; processes do only if they escaped a `BestEffort` teardown. Output is never stored.

interrupt_requested.description: Stays set on a `running` process that can't be killed.

Reason.description: Why `state` differs from `desired`. Latched: no action until acknowledged.

version.description: Bumped by every accepted write; send it as `if_version`.

Status.description: `running` is set when compute is created. Converged: `state` equals `desired`, or a `reason` is set. After a daemon restart, a running sandbox becomes `stopped` with a `reason`.

state.description: Same values, or `null` before the first commit.
